newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 shows modest gain awaiting Dow.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 shows modest gain awaiting Dow.

text.p: The FTSE 100 held on to modest gains ahead of the U.S. opening on Thursday, looking for fresh incentive from the Dow, which was expected to open mixed.
The leading index was up 8.7 points at 4,883.2 by 1243 GMT, with advancers in a slim majority. The market had see-sawed during the morning, struggling to find a clear direction.

Wall Street stocks were seen opening mixed but vulnerable to profit-taking after two consecutive record closes, dealer said. U.S. weekly jobless claims which came in weaker-than-expected were seen having limited impact despite briefly sending the S&P index futures and U.S. bonds into negative territory.

Second-line UK stocks were still trailing in the doldrums after a Confederation of British Industry survey added to already strong evidence that sterling's seeming inexorable rise is badly affecting corporate Britain.
The Mid-250 was down 2.1 points at 4,479.7. But leading stocks had managed to recover some poise in volatile trade after dipping to lows of 4,855.4.
The survey showed British manufacturers' export orders in the four months to July fell at the fastest rate since October 1991, the middle of the last recession.
The CBI's quarterly trends survey showed domestic demand rose at the fastest rate since April 1995, although overall growth of orders slowed.

"The survey is telling us what we already know - that we have a two-speed economy and that makes the interest rate decision very difficult," said Panmure Gordon equities strategist, Ian Williams. "It's a traders' market," he added.
Among stock features there were several sharp price movements. A 4.5 percent price rise for MAM was described by one dealer as a "gutless squeeze" -- a big movement in thin trade.
Dealers said demand for the stock stemmed from its recent underperformance. MAM climbed 58-1/2p to 13.38-1/2 stg.
Bass and other UK brewers rose after a report that Carlsberg-Tetley planned to close at least one UK brewery led to hopes that overcapacity in the industry may ease. Bass gained 15p to 854p.
Shares in Centrica rose 5-1/2p to 86-1/4p as dealers noted switching from BG Plc which eased 2p to 239-1/2p.
Shares in Railtrack greeted the group's AGM by setting a new all-time high of 805p before easing to be up 14p at 799.
Elsewhere, ICI shed 14p to 911p after the group confirmed a steep drop in half-year profits and Boots fell 29p to 787p on disappointing sales news.
